gaps.lead: The police believe the two suspects left the country.
gaps.explanation: A present belief about a past event: are believed to have + participle.

gaps.lead: There isn't a single clean cup left in the cupboard.
gaps.hint: run out of = have none left
gaps.explanation: run out of = have no more of something left.

gaps.lead: No changes will be made to this project.
gaps.hint: go ahead = proceed; according to plan
gaps.explanation: 'No changes' means the project 'will go ahead according to plan'.

gaps.lead: I'd prefer it if you arrived before eight.
gaps.explanation: would rather + subject + past simple for other people's actions.

gaps.lead: She cooked a huge meal, but we had already eaten.
gaps.explanation: needn't have + participle = it happened although it wasn't necessary.

gaps.lead: 'I'll definitely call you when I land,' she told me.
gaps.explanation: Reported promise: promised to call; the person promised shifts to 'me'.
